_comment: CASE 1A -- PARTIAL PARTICIPATION, MILP (single-path) leg. Same topology, same active set, same clock and same objective as mini_1gpu_1nic_alltoall_partial_1A.json, solved with the chunk-level MILP (formulation 1) at num_chunks 1 so each (src, dst) pair owns exactly ONE indivisible 1 GB chunk that takes exactly ONE path end to end. That is the no-multipath regime a ring-style algorithm gives you, except the solver still picks the BEST such assignment -- so LP-minus-MILP is a LOWER bound on what per-pair multipath is worth, not an upper one.
_pipeline_timing: FIXED (branch milp-bottleneck-pipeline, 2026-10-12) -- the MILP's cut-through timing used to be OPTIMISTIC here: it credited a switch traversal with its FIRST link's beta, so at this pinned 0.08 s epoch (one chunk on a 100Gbps port, half a chunk on the 50Gbps uplink) a chunk crossing a spine was credited in 0.08 s while it physically needs 0.16 s, and the fast link was freed while the slow one still drained it. allgather.py now gives every link touching a switch a PACE CLASS -- the beta of its traversal's slowest link -- so a traversal holds all its links at the bottleneck rate and lands when the bottleneck has carried it. The MILP's 3-Epochs_Required / 4-Collective_Finish_Time / 5-Algo_Bandwidth are now physically achievable and optimal on the epoch grid; teccl/solvers/milp_pipeline_check.py checks both. Measured (MILP, before -> after): 1A 0.08 -> 0.16 s; 2B 0.32 -> 0.32 s, but the old schedule needed twice the link capacity it claimed; 2C 0.72 -> 0.80 s, the single-path bound (9 whole chunks cross two 50Gbps uplinks, so one carries 5 x 0.16 s). The LP was never affected (it splits chunks; 2C's LP 0.72 s is that split).
_participation: active GPUs [0, 2]; passive GPUs [1, 3]. GPU index == node index (gpu0..gpu3 = nodes 0..3; leaf0/leaf1 = 4/5; spine0/spine1 = 6/7); gpu0,gpu1 home on leaf0 and gpu2,gpu3 on leaf1, so the active pair is one GPU per leaf and both demands are cross-leaf. A passive GPU still exists and may RELAY -- gpu1 can forward for gpu0 -- it just sources and sinks no demand of its own. num_chunks 1 means one chunk per (src, dst) PAIR; Scheduler._scale_alltoall_num_chunks widens the chunk axis by the ACTIVE count only, so the instance is 2 chunks, not 12.
_vs_lp: Differences from mini_1gpu_1nic_alltoall_partial_1A.json, and only these: formulation 1 (MILP) not 2 (LP); symmetry false not true; num_epochs 8 in both; distinct log_file and schedule_output_file so neither run clobbers the other. Held fixed: topo_file, passive_node_indices, chunk_size 1, collective 2, num_chunks 1, switch_copy false, epoch_type 3 / epoch_duration 0.08 (pinned, identical in both), switch_pipeline true, solution_method 1, time_limit 2. ALSO DIFFERENT: objective_type 2 (TOTAL_DEMAND) here against the LP's 6 (LEXICOGRAPHIC) -- so the difference is integrality PLUS objective, not integrality alone; it is still not granularity. See _objective_note for exactly what that trades.
_objective_note: OBJECTIVE: TOTAL_DEMAND (objective_type 2), NOT the lexicographic 6 the LP partner uses. WHAT IT IS: allgather.py::objective_formulation builds -100 * sum_k max(sum_(s,d,c) total_demand_sat[s][d][c][k] - (Demand - 1), 0). The inner term is 1 exactly when EVERY demand is already satisfied by the end of epoch k and 0 otherwise, so the objective pays 100 per epoch of the horizon that the collective has already finished in -- i.e. it MINIMIZES THE COMPLETION EPOCH directly. That is the point of using it here: '3-Epochs_Required' becomes the quantity the solver is actually optimizing, so a reported makespan can be compared against the analytic bound as a real optimality claim rather than as an artifact of where a latency-sum objective happened to leave the last straggler. WHAT IT GIVES UP -- read this before judging the routing: objective_type 6 carried two lower-priority tiers that 2 does not have. Tier 2 penalized HOST RELAY (volume a GPU forwards on behalf of another GPU) and tier 3 penalized SWITCH-CHAIN LENGTH (flow entering a switch: 0 for a direct link, 1 for gpu->switch->gpu, 3 for a leaf->spine->leaf detour). Under objective 2 the solver is INDIFFERENT among all schedules that finish in the same epoch, so expect gratuitous relays and spine detours that carry no cost -- the schedule stays correct and makespan-optimal, but it is no longer the tidiest routing that achieves that makespan, and a relay or a long chain in the output is no longer evidence that it was needed. MIDDLE GROUND if that matters: objective_type 5 (TOTAL_DEMAND_MIN_SWITCH_HOPS) is this same completion reward plus a GAMMA=1e-4 per-unit penalty on switch->switch flow, small enough never to trade completion time for hops, which restores a shortest-chain preference (but still no relay tier). COST: the objective adds two continuous aux vars and one max_ general constraint per epoch, which is negligible next to the (source, link, chunk, epoch) flow variables. COMPARABILITY CAVEAT: the LP partner still uses objective_type 6, so the LP-vs-MILP difference is no longer integrality ALONE -- it is integrality plus objective. For the makespan that is fine (both are measured against the same analytic lower bound, which neither objective can beat); for a ROUTING diff, remember the LP is tie-broken toward fewer relays and shorter switch chains and this MILP is not.
_why_symmetry_off: symmetry true adds an orbit-averaging projection that is free on the LP -- the feasible set is convex, so the symmetric average of an optimum is an optimum -- but is a REAL restriction on the integral problem, where an equal split across an orbit need not exist at the integral optimum. Cutting off that optimum is precisely the measurement error this file exists to avoid, so it is off and the reported makespan is the true single-path optimum.
_expected: The correct single-path answer is 0.16 s = 2 epochs: the chunk is indivisible, so it rides ONE 50Gbps uplink, and 1 GB / 6.25 GB/s = 0.16 s = ceil(chunk / min bandwidth on the path) = 1 + max(beta) epochs. MEASURED since the pace-class fix: 0.16 s, both chunks in pace class 1 (before it, the solver reported 0.08 s by charging the traversal only its fast first hop; see _pipeline_timing). WHAT TO INSPECT: each direction's chunk should appear on ONE spine and never be split, against the LP partner's 0.5/0.5 fan across both -- that difference is integrality, it is real, and it is visible in 8-Chunk paths regardless of the timing defect. Relaying through the passive GPU buys nothing (it does not widen the leaf cut) -- but under objective_type 2 nothing PENALIZES it either, so a detour through gpu1 or gpu3 may appear and is not a bug; it just means the solver was indifferent. Under the LP partner's objective 6 the relay tier would have removed it.
_epoch_note: epoch_type 3 (USER_INPUT) with epoch_duration PINNED to 0.08 s = 1 GB / 12.5 GB/s, one 100Gbps host port. Deliberately NOT the SLOWEST_LINK value (0.16 s, the 50Gbps uplink) that the full-participation files on this topology use: at 0.16 s the LP's answer is rounded up to the epoch grid, and pinning 0.08 s is what makes the LP's makespan land exactly on its true bound. The MILP leg used to pay for it with an optimistic reported time; since the pace-class fix it does not (see _pipeline_timing). Both legs share this clock so the routing comparison stays controlled. For this leg specifically the pin is what exercises the pace classes: the 50Gbps uplink has beta 1 here (at 0.16 s every beta is 0 and the old and new timing agree).
_horizon_note: num_epochs is the MILP's time horizon and it costs -- one integer flow variable per (source, link, chunk, epoch) -- so it is kept tight: the bound below is 1 epoch and 4 leaves ample headroom. If the solve comes back INFEASIBLE rather than merely slow, raise this first; an infeasible horizon and a hard instance look nothing alike in the Gurobi log. With objective_type 2 the horizon no longer DISTORTS the answer, only the model size: the reward is paid per epoch in which the whole collective is already complete, so a larger num_epochs just widens the reward range and the solver still drives the completion epoch down. Contrast objective_type 6, under which the reported makespan was only an upper bound (its tier 1 minimizes the SUM of completion epochs, not the max, so a straggler could drift late inside a generous horizon) -- see _objective_note.
_topology_note: The topology comes from the .topo DSL file; topo_file SELECTS it, so TECCLSolver.get_topology builds a DslTopology and `name` is only the free-form label for output filenames and the Gurobi log. The path is relative to the repo root.
